title: Ab initio thermodynamic statistical modeling of the miscibility gap and the metal-insulator phase transition in SrTi$_{1-x}$V$_x$O$_{3}$
authors: Luka Wibmer, Chiara Ostendorf, Dominik Spath, Christoph Heil, Pedro N. Ferreira, Markus Aichhorn
abstract: The substitutional alloy SrTi$_{1-x}$V$_x$O$_3$ interpolates between the band insulator SrTiO$_3$ and the correlated metal SrVO$_3$, exhibiting a composition-driven metal--insulator transition whose origin combines Mott physics with local chemical disorder. Previous first-principles studies relied on individual supercells, which cannot capture the thermally disordered solid solution, since configurations of identical composition can display very different electronic properties. Here we treat the alloy within a generalized quasi-chemical approximation, a thermodynamically consistent statistical framework in which every property is obtained as an ensemble average over all symmetry-inequivalent clusters, weighted by occurrence probabilities that minimize the Gibbs mixing free energy. This provides a well-defined procedure to average over different supercells, and places the structural and electronic descriptions on an equal footing. From the mixing thermodynamics we obtain a miscibility gap with a critical temperature of 1443 K, consistent with experimental evidence. Combining the cluster ensemble with dynamical mean-field theory, we track the density of states at the Fermi level across the full composition range: whereas density-functional theory alone predicts a metal for all $x>0$, the correlated spectral function reproduces the transition, evolving from insulating below $x\approx0.3$ to metallic near $x=1$. Finally, classifying clusters as metallic or insulating and performing site percolation on a simple cubic lattice yields a sharp onset of system-spanning conduction near $x\approx0.4$. These results establish a thermodynamically consistent, configuration--averaged framework applicable to the broader class of correlated materials.
summary: This work develops a thermodynamically rigorous framework, the Generalized Quasi-Chemical Approximation (GQCA), to model disordered alloys like SrTi1-xV xO3. By averaging properties over all possible atomic arrangements, the authors accurately predict both the miscibility gap and the composition-driven metal-insulator transition using DMFT and percolation theory.
main_problem: The study addresses the composition-driven metal-insulator transition (MIT) and miscibility gap in the disordered perovskite alloy SrTi1-xV xO3.
main_result: The authors successfully reproduce the MIT using a thermodynamically consistent, configuration-averaged framework, finding the transition onset near x=0.4 via percolation analysis.
method: They employ the Generalized Quasi-Chemical Approximation (GQCA) combined with Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) to average properties over all possible atomic configurations.
model_or_system: The system is the substitutional solid solution SrTi1-xV xO3, which interpolates between a band insulator (SrTiO3) and a correlated metal (SrVO3). The model treats disorder by averaging cluster properties weighted by Gibbs free energy minimization.
key_observables: Miscibility gap critical temperature (1443 K), density of states at the Fermi level, and system-spanning conduction onset via site percolation.
important_parameters: The Hubbard interaction parameters (U=4 eV, J=0.65 eV) are used in the DMFT calculation; the analysis spans the full composition range x from 0 to 1.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that material properties can be accurately calculated as an ensemble average over statistically weighted clusters using the GQCA framework, which overcomes limitations of single supercell calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice parameter following Vegard's law and show the miscibility gap boundaries derived from $\Delta G(x, T)$ analysis. Partial density of states plots demonstrate bandwidth changes as composition varies.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for a configuration-averaged approach (GQCA) to model disorder. It then calculates thermodynamic properties ($\Delta G$) revealing the miscibility gap. Finally, it combines this ensemble average with DMFT and percolation theory to track the electronic transition across the composition range.
why_interesting: The methodology of using statistical thermodynamics (GQCA) to correctly average over local chemical disorder when modeling correlated electron systems is highly relevant for understanding complex materials where structural randomness dictates electronic behavior, bridging concepts from condensed matter stat-mech and strongly correlated physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Lattice parameter a of SrTi1−xVxO3 as a function of com- position. Both the GQCA average and experimental measurements [8–10] are depicted. The gray shaded area shows the GQCA stan- dard deviation.

Figure 2. Thermodynamic properties of SrTi1−xVxO3 as a function of composition. (a) Excess enthalpies ∆j. (b) Mixing enthalpy ∆H, (c) configurational entropy T∆S and (d) Gibbs mixing free energy ∆G at different Temperatures from 400 K to 2000 K. (e) The miscibility gap with binodal and spinodal lines.

Fig. 2(e) shows the calculated miscibility gap for SrTi1−xVxO3. We predict a critical temperature of 1443 K. Experimental information on the phase equilibria of this sys- tem is rather limited. As far as we could identify, no thermo- dynamic assessment or phase diagram has been reported for the Sr–Ti–V–O quaternary system. SrTi1−xVxO3 solid solu- tions have been synthesized using several different methods, including powders treated at 1250 K under flowing H2 fol- lowed by hydrostatic pressing [8], solid-state synthesis of pel- lets heated at T ≈1800 K [9], and different thin-film growth techniques [10–12].

Figure 3. Electronic density of states at the Fermi level taken from the DFT calculation and the spectral function A(ω) at ω = 0 of SrTi1−xVxO3 as a function of composition. Both the GQCA aver- age and the individual cluster values are plotted. The gray shaded area shows the GQCA standard deviation.

Figure 4. Vanadium-projected GQCA averaged spectral function A(ω) for different compositions x in SrTi1−xVxO3. Each spectral function is shifted vertically by 0.1 eV−1 for better visibility. Note that only the vanadium-projected part is shown, that is why for x = 0.0 the spectral function is identically zero.
